prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that your truck is a rental. Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the Cookout Division,

I appear before this committee today not to evade, but to clarify. The allegation that my vehicle is a rental has been presented as evidence of subversive potluck activity, but I submit to you that this is a fundamental mischaracterization of both my transportation and my patriotism.

Yes, the vehicle in question was procured through Enterprise Rent-A-Car. But I ask this committee: since when did fiscal prudence become un-American? Since when did the responsible use of a weekend rate with unlimited mileage become a threat to our sacred tradition of backyard fellowship?

My truck may be a rental, but my commitment to the cookout is owned outright. I have transported no fewer than four coolers of ice, two folding tables, and a propane grill in that bed. I have hauled charcoal briquettes across county lines. I have arrived early to secure parking and stayed late to assist with cleanup. These are not the actions of a transient saboteur; these are the actions of a dedicated citizen of the cul-de-sac.

Furthermore, I would direct the committee’s attention to the fact that I *returned* the truck with a full tank of gas and no damage to the interior. Is this not the very essence of civic responsibility? Had I been engaged in un-American activities, would I not have left crumbs on the upholstery or returned it fifteen minutes past the grace period?

The real question this committee should be asking is not whether my truck is rented, but whether my potato salad was made with store-bought mayonnaise. *That* is where true scrutiny belongs. On the matter of the vehicle, I stand by my record: I rented responsibly, I hauled honorably, and I returned it on time.

I yield my remaining time to the gentleman from Ohio, who I believe still owes this committee an explanation regarding his use of paper plates at last month’s event.
